proposal.hypothesis: The ACT policy's first weakness in manipulated-object generalization is spatial: translating the bell within a bounded reachable workspace will reduce official press success or increase final bell-contact distance relative to the unchanged control.

requested_perturbation.description: Create one scene variant that translates the bell to a bounded, reachable position while leaving its appearance, geometry, contact point, and all other scene elements unchanged.

task_need.description: TaskGen must create a bounded object_position variant overlay for the bell and preserve the official click_bell success contract.

tool_need.description: ToolGen should reuse the official success checker and generate a rule metric reporting the final target-contact distance and whether the active gripper is closed, so partial spatial degradation is observable even if the binary outcome remains successful.

proposal.rationale: The unchanged control succeeds, so it does not reveal a generalization boundary. A bounded bell translation is the most direct supported test of whether ACT depends on the demonstrated object location, while preserving object identity and appearance and adding contact-distance observability to distinguish spatial degradation from unrelated failure.
